metadata.title: Trump admin. urges Apple not to purchase Chinese memory chips, but this presents a problem

content.text:
US Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick says the Trump administration does not want Apple (AAPL) to purchase memory chips from China.
Yahoo Finance Technology Editor Dan Howley explains why this presents issues for Apple.

US Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick says the Trump administration does not want Apple (AAPL) to purchase memory chips from China.
Yahoo Finance Technology Editor Dan Howley explains why this presents issues for Apple.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick saying the Trump administration does not want Apple buying memory chips from China. Explain the problem Apple is dealing with here, Dan.
Yeah, so basically memory is, you know, incredibly hard to come by. Uh, storage is incredibly hard to come by. Uh, China has two memory makers uh that uh Apple could lean on and try to purchase memory from kind of, you know, to offset some of the the price increases or at least ensure that they have adequate supply to meet the demand that they have.
Now, the the US government says that those companies uh have ties to uh, you know, the Chinese military, uh and that uh if they uh Apple went ahead and used them, they would also be undercutting American companies uh like Micron when it comes to to memory. Uh obviously Micron's been doing very well as a result of this AI blowout uh uh buildout. Uh and so they would love to obviously keep that going, uh and they've also kind of been lobbying to not allow Apple to to be able to purchase these kinds of chips.
But, you know, I think for for Apple what it comes down to is trying to control costs, ensuring that they have the products that their consumers want, uh and being able to do that uh as freely as they can.
Now, it it looks as though they would not ship uh devices equipped with Chinese uh made memory into the US, it would just be for for the Chinese market. And uh according to the report, uh HP has already done something similar. Uh and so, you know, obviously they're also dealing with the same kind of memory shortage.
And so, we we kind of just have to see what Apple decides to do. They've they've done a great job uh so far of kind of, you know, working with the Trump administration to avoid uh any kind of unnecessary upsets uh as far as their their business practices go. Um, you know, especially when it came to to tariffs, but this could be something that put them back on the Trump administration's radar.
